'''Gabriel Peyré''' (born 1979)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.idref.fr/077078128|title=Peyré, Gabriel (1979-....)|website=idref.fr|access-date=19 July 2021}}</ref> is a French [[mathematician]]. Most of his work lies in the field of [[Transportation theory (mathematics)|transportation theory]]. He is a [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|CNRS]] senior researcher and a Professor in the mathematics and applications department of the [[École normale supérieure (Paris)|École normale supérieure]] in Paris.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Contact - Homepage of Gabriel Peyré|url=http://www.gpeyre.com/contact/|access-date=24 March 2021|website=www.gpeyre.com}}</ref> He was awarded the [[CNRS Silver Medal]] in 2021.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Gabriel Peyré {{!}} CNRS|url=https://www.cnrs.fr/fr/personne/gabriel-peyre|access-date=2022-01-17|website=www.cnrs.fr|date=11 March 2021 |language=fr}}</ref>

==Life and work==

His work mainly focuses on applied mathematics, in particular on the [[Imaging|imaging sciences]] and [[machine learning]] applications of [[Transportation theory (mathematics)|optimal transport]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=[Webinar] Gabriel Peyré ran a Seminar@SystemX on June 17, 2020 {{!}} IRT SystemX|url=https://www.irt-systemx.fr/en/evenements/webinar-gabriel-peyre-will-run-a-seminarsystemx-on-june-17-2020/|access-date=4 March 2021|language=en-US}}</ref>

Gabriel Peyré is also the deputy director of the 3IA Paris [[Artificial intelligence|Artificial Intelligence]] Research Institute<ref>{{Cite web|date=2019-09-26|title=Governance {{!}} Prairie|url=https://prairie-institute.fr/governance/|access-date=2021-03-24|language=en-GB}}</ref> as well as a member of the scientific committee of the [[École normale supérieure (Paris)|ENS]] center for data science.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Data @ ENS - ENS-CFM Data Science Chair|url=https://data-ens.github.io/|access-date=2021-03-24|website=data-ens.github.io}}</ref> He is also the creator of the Numerical tour of data science,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Numerical Tours - A Numerical Tour of Data Science|url=https://www.numerical-tours.com/|access-date=24 March 2021|website=www.numerical-tours.com}}</ref> a popular online repository of Python/Matlab/Julia/R resources to teach mathematical data sciences. He is a frequent collaborator of the [[National Centre for Scientific Research|INRIA]] team Mokaplan.<ref name="Inria">{{cite web |title=Mokaplan |url=https://team.inria.fr/mokaplan/ |website=Inria |date=21 July 2011 |access-date=25 May 2021}}</ref>

==Awards and distinctions==
Gabriel Peyré was awarded the Blaise Pascal Prize in 2017 from the [[French Academy of Sciences|Académie des sciences]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=Les prix de l'Académie des sciences 2017|url=https://www.academie-sciences.fr/pdf/documentation/prix2017/plaquette_prix_2017/index.html#89|access-date=24 March 2021|website=www.academie-sciences.fr}}</ref> as well as the Enrico Magenes Prize (2019) from the [[Italian Mathematical Union|Unione Matematica Italiana]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Premio "Enrico Magenes" – Sito dell'Unione Matematica Italiana|url=https://umi.dm.unibo.it/premi-old/premio-enrico-magenes/|access-date=2021-03-24|language=it-IT}}</ref> He also was an invited speaker at the [[European Congress of Mathematics]] in 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|title=8th European Congress of Mathematics|url=https://www.8ecm.si/program/plenary-speakers/36|access-date=24 March 2021|website=8th European Congress of Mathematics}}</ref> His research was supported by an [[European Research Council#Grants offered|ERC starting grant]] in 2012 and by an [[European Research Council#Grants offered|ERC consolidator grant]] in 2017.<ref>{{Cite web|title=NORIA - Homepage of Gabriel Peyré|url=http://www.gpeyre.com/noria/|access-date=24 March 2021|website=www.gpeyre.com}}</ref> In 2021, he was awarded the CNRS Silver Medal.<ref name=":0" />
